name: Refugee Council: advocacy and awareness raising (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: UK asylum and refugee policy, for people in the UK asylum system.
summary: The Refugee Council's advocacy and awareness raising (research, policy, parliamentary work, campaigns, media and its new brand: £4.3m over the two years to March 2025) is counted as a past average against what those years won: the government's pilot doubling the move-on period for newly recognised refugees from 28 to 56 days (from December 2024; ended for single adults in September 2025), and the restart of asylum processing with the Rwanda plan scrapped. Valued as extra days of housing and support for about 31,600 refugees a year over the pilot and as claims decided instead of left in limbo for about 29,000 arrivals a year, with 30% of the move-on change and 5% of the other caused by campaigning, the Refugee Council's share of the campaigners 25% and 12%, and its next dollar at 42% of the average, a dollar does about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000 (plausible range {{range}}). That is low because the people helped are in the UK and most of the change came from the new government's own plans. The result is mostly judgment (how much of each win campaigning caused spans ten-fold) and is discounted for missing data; any lasting change to the move-on period after March 2025 is left for the next year's accounts.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

source.title: British Refugee Council (Refugee Council), Trustees Annual Report and Accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 (audited; Charity Commission register, charity 1014576)

rows.explainer: The six charitable lines, support costs included.

rows.label: Total expenses
Program expenses
Overhead multiplier (total ÷ program expenses)
rows.explainer: Support costs are already in each line; this spreads fundraising over the lines by cost (the 2024/25 ratio for both years).

rows.label: Cost of the two years' advocacy, including overhead
People granted protection or other leave at initial decision in a year

source.title: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending March 2025: How many people are granted asylum in the UK?
source.quote: In the year ending March 2025, 45,084 people were granted refugee protection or other leave at initial decision

rows.explainer: Main applicants and dependants: the people who move on from asylum support when their claim is granted. 45,084 in the year to March 2025, 35% fewer than the year before; the range runs from a slower year to the previous year's pace.

rows.label: Share of them in Home Office asylum support when granted
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (50-85%): most people seeking asylum have no other means and live in Home Office accommodation (hotels or dispersed housing); some live with family or friends, and children in council care don't move on from asylum support.

rows.label: Refugees moving on from asylum support a year
Extra days in asylum support during the 56-day pilot (median)

source.title: Home Office, Evaluation of the initiatives to enhance the move on process (June 2026)
source.quote: the median time from asylum decision to support exit rose from 41 days before the pilot to 56 days after the pilot

rows.explainer: The government's evaluation compares six months before and after the pilot began: the median stay after a decision rose by 15 days (41 to 56); the move-on period itself doubled from 28 to 56 days, but many stayed beyond 28 days before (reinstatements, slow exits).

rows.label: Years the 56-day period applied

source.title: Home Office, Evaluation of the initiatives to enhance the move on process (June 2026)
source.quote: the pilot extending the move on period from 28 to 56 days ended on 1 September 2025 for single adults

rows.explainer: From 9 December 2024 to 1 September 2025 for single adults (0.73 years); families, pregnant women, people over 65 and disabled people kept 56 days after that (up to about 1.25 years). Most refugees moving on are single adults: 0.85 (0.72-1.25).

rows.label: Value of a day of asylum support (housing and allowance) to the person (£)

source.title: GOV.UK, Asylum support: what you'll get
source.quote: You'll usually get £49.18 for each person in your household.

rows.explainer: Judgment £25 (£15-40): the allowance (£49.18 a week, £7 a day, gov.uk) and a roof valued at the cheapest room the person could otherwise rent (£13-23 a night outside London, more in London), never what the Home Office pays for a hotel bed; for those who would have been homeless without the extra days, the roof is the gain.

rows.label: Newly recognised refugees' consumption per person (US$)
rows.explainer: The UK survey average × the shared share for people in the asylum system, as charityevals' model of the Refugee Council's services reads it.

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per person-year of extra support
rows.explainer: The value used up over t years gains t × ln(1 + v ÷ (b × t)); v ÷ t is a year's worth at the daily value, so the gain is t × this row.

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per refugee from the pilot's extra days
ln(consumption) gain per refugee per year from a lasting change to the move-on period
rows.explainer: 0: the pilot ended for single adults in September 2025, and any later lasting change falls after the two years whose spending is counted (Convention 11: cost and wins from the same period); it is counted when the next year's accounts are modelled. The pilot's own spell is counted above.

rows.label: Refugees moving on each year
The pilot's units of value (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Each year's refugees under the pilot × the gain × its years (a short, fixed spell, not the site's years for a lasting reform).

rows.label: People arriving by small boat a year

source.title: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending December 2024: How many people come to the UK irregularly?
source.quote: In 2024, 36,816 people arrived in the UK on small boats, 25% more than in 2023 (29,437).

rows.explainer: The people the Illegal Migration Act 2023's duty to remove would have left with claims never decided (it applied to everyone arriving irregularly after 7 March 2023 who came through a safe country), to be removed to Rwanda or kept in limbo.

rows.label: Share of them the Act would have kept from a decision
rows.explainer: Judgment 80% (60-95%): unaccompanied children were exempt until 18, and a few would have been removed to their own country or a third country; the rest would have been in limbo. IPPR estimated up to 55,500 already stuck in a 'perma-backlog' by early 2024.

rows.label: Life satisfaction gained by having a claim decided instead of indefinite limbo (points)
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.4 points (0.1-1): the Refugee Council's own repeated surveys of about 800 clients find people in the asylum system far less likely than refugees to report improvements (31% against 55% more confident dealing with unexpected events, 20% against 45% worrying less, p. 14), and the report puts it down to the asylum system's uncertainty and insecurity; anchor at the high end: in panel surveys of refugees in Germany and Australia, separation from family is among the largest falls in life satisfaction (about a point), a larger change than a decision on a claim. The gain is for everyone covered: those granted gain status, those refused at least a decision; the right to work and benefits that come with status are in this gain, not counted again.

rows.label: Years of limbo avoided per person
rows.explainer: Judgment 1.5 years (6 months to 3 years): without the change, claims would have stayed undecided until a later government, a court ruling or removal; the legacy backlog of 2022-23 took about two years to clear.

rows.label: WELLBYs per person covered
Life satisfaction gained per person covered (points, as a year's equivalent)
rows.explainer: The limbo avoided, in WELLBYs per person, entered per year of arrivals.

rows.label: People a year whose claims are decided because of the change
Health per person (DALYs)
rows.explainer: 0: the health effects of status and of not being removed to Rwanda are in the life-satisfaction gain; no deaths are counted (the Rwanda plan removed no one against their will before it was scrapped).

rows.label: Chance the wins happen
rows.explainer: 1: the model counts wins that have happened; whether they would have come anyway is the counterfactual, asked once (Convention 5).

rows.label: Years a won reform counts
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (Your values; docs/normalization.md 2.9). The pilot's own years are counted separately above.

rows.label: Years until the wins take effect
rows.explainer: Judgment a quarter of a year (0 to 9 months): the government restarted processing in July 2024 and the pilot began in December 2024.

rows.label: Wait discounted
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Discounted years of a won reform
People released (casework)
rows.explainer: 0: the advocacy line doesn't do casework; the services' legal and age-dispute help is in charityevals' model of the Refugee Council's services.

rows.label: Years released (unused)
rows.explainer: Unused while released_people is 0; the template's figure, kept so the shared casework rows stay intact.

rows.label: Life satisfaction gained per year released (unused)
rows.explainer: Unused while released_people is 0; the template's figure, kept so the shared casework rows stay intact.

rows.label: WELLBYs per person released
Evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.85 (0.6-1): the counts are official and the pilot's extra days measured; the value of the days and of a decision are judgments with their own ranges. This adjusts for the evaluation's before-after design (other changes, the eVisa rollout, overlapped the pilot).

rows.label: Move-on: share of the win caused by the campaign
rows.explainer: Judgment 30% (10-60%): the Refugee Council and partners campaigned for a 56-day move-on period for years and published research on refugee homelessness in the year (p. 15); the new government piloted it within months of taking office after a letter from the sector, and a homelessness duty of 56 days already applied to everyone else, so some of the change would have come anyway. Anchor: Baumgartner et al. (2009, Lobbying and Policy Change) find most campaigns change nothing, and those that win share the credit with officials' own plans.

rows.label: Processing restarted and Rwanda scrapped: share caused by the campaign
rows.explainer: Judgment 5% (1-15%): both were in the winning party's manifesto, so the election decided them; the campaigning's part is the arguments and costings the new ministers used ('clear on the immediate steps needed', p. 15) and keeping the plan from starting before the election.

rows.label: Move-on: the Refugee Council's share of the coalition's resources
rows.explainer: Judgment 25% (10-45%): the move-on campaign was led by a coalition (NACCOM, the British Red Cross, Crisis, St Mungo's, Homeless Link, councils through the Local Government Association); the Refugee Council is one of the largest refugee charities in it.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: Move-on: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among those who paid for or did the same work, times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out or adopt the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Processing and Rwanda: the Refugee Council's share of the campaigners' resources
rows.explainer: Judgment 12% (5-25%): many organisations opposed the Act and the Rwanda plan (Amnesty, the Refugee Council, Freedom from Torture, Care4Calais, the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants, lawyers who litigated it, the UNHCR); the Refugee Council's costings and reports were among the most cited.

rows.label: Processing and Rwanda: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among those who paid for or did the same work, times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out or adopt the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome (outcome-weighted average)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only: each branch applies its own row.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches' used shares, for reading only: each branch applies its own.

rows.label: Share caused (outcome-weighted average)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only: each branch applies its own row.

rows.label: Share of the wins enforced
rows.explainer: Judgment 95% (80-100%): the extra days were measured in the stays themselves and processing did restart; some refugees still left support early or were evicted on the old timetable.

rows.label: Counted less for missing outcome data
rows.explainer: Thin: the wins are counted, but what they changed for people (the value of extra days, of a decision) and the campaign's part are judgments with no measurement. Counted less by the shared slider (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Move-on: adjustments combined
Processing and Rwanda: adjustments combined
All adjustments combined (outcome-weighted average)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only: each branch applies its own row.

rows.label: Side effect: the year's smaller wins
rows.explainer: The Bibby Stockholm barge (about 400 men) closed, family reunion extended for Afghan refugees, the Childhood First Partnership's age-assessment toolkit, the All-Party Parliamentary Group's inquiry on safe routes (p. 15-16): each smaller or less clearly the campaign's than the two wins modelled. 5% (1-15%) of the modelled result.

rows.label: Side effect: public attitudes and backlash
rows.explainer: The new brand, Fair Shot campaign (1.6 million social media users reached) and 7,000 media mentions (p. 17) may soften attitudes to refugees, which helps future campaigns and refugees' welcome; high-profile campaigning can also harden opponents. +2% (-3% to +8%).

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: The signed side effects above, each read at the shared side-effect weight.

rows.label: Move-on: units of value (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: A lasting change over the site's years for a won reform (0 here, see ln_gain_per_person_year), plus the pilot's spell.

rows.label: Income gained, in units of value (after adjustments)
Income gained, in healthy years
rows.explainer: The bridge from UoV into healthy years (docs/normalization.md 2.6): fixed, don't edit.

rows.label: Processing and Rwanda: WELLBYs (before adjustments)
Life satisfaction gained, in WELLBYs (after adjustments)
Life satisfaction gained, in healthy years
rows.explainer: The bridge from WELLBYs into healthy years (docs/normalization.md 2.6): fixed, don't edit.

rows.label: Move-on before adjustments, in healthy years
rows.explainer: The fixed bridge, for the weights of the averages.

rows.label: Processing and Rwanda before adjustments, in healthy years
rows.explainer: The fixed bridge, for the weights of the averages.

rows.label: Healthy years counted directly
Years of healthy life
rows.explainer: Both wins, each after its own adjustments, plus the side effects.
